newsitem.title: POLAND: Hungarian, Polish leaders map future cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian, Polish leaders map future cooperation.

text.p: Hungary and Poland agreed on Tuesday that the European Union and NATO should negotiate separately with aspirants for membership as candidate countries were at different stages of preparation.
Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn and his Polish counterpart Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz agreed, however, to hold diplomatic consultations on their common goal of EU entry, PAP news agency reported.

Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski, who also met Horn, stressed that "between the two countries there was no competition in aspirations to joining the EU and NATO," his office said in a communique.

Hungary and Poland are generally acknowledged to be in the front rank of future NATO members, along with the Czech Republic. U.S. President Bill Clinton has said the first new members will be brought into the defence alliance in 1999.
The complex process of EU admission, also eagerly sought by both countries, is set to take longer.
PAP said Horn and Cimoszewicz, speaking to reporters after their talks, called for Slovakia to be able to enter negotiations on joining the EU and NATO.
Horn also proposed a bilateral meeting during the first half of 1997 to discuss possibilities for cooperation in production.
He approved Poland's steps towards liberalisation of its trade relations with Russia, initiated during Cimoszewicz's visit to Moscow last week.
"Hungary is aiming for the same thing, because without this Hungarian-Russian economic links will not proceed," he said.

The countries have also signed an agreement on academic and technical cooperation. Before leaving on Wednesday, Horn is to visit Poland's Roman Catholic Primate, Cardinal Jozef Glemp and meet parliamentary speakers.
